Package model.description.abstraction

Class AbstractDescribed

java.lang.Object
model.logic.abstraction.AbstractFormal
model.description.abstraction.AbstractDescribed
All Implemented Interfaces:
Comparable<Formal>, Described, Formal
Direct Known Subclasses:
DPrimitive
public abstract class AbstractDescribed extends AbstractFormal implements Described
Provides the basic functionality for classes that meet the Described interface. Constructors and clones is not provided.

    • description

      public DRectangle description()
      The graphical part of a formal's description. Remember that a lot other things could be included in the description of a piece of mathematics such as gradings and checks of different sorts.
      Specified by:
      description in interface Described
      Returns:
      A functionally very enriched rectangle describing this formal. DRectangle is a very central class in this application, it is the center of nearly all graphics.

    • getLocalReference

      public Point2D.Double getLocalReference()
      Returns the local referencepoint which points to the reference point, the start of the base line if the upper left corner of the glyph is situated at origo. Consider that machine device coordinates always have origo in upper left corner. This differ probably from common typography.
      Specified by:
      getLocalReference in interface Described
      Returns:
      The vector offset from the upper left corner to the glyph's base line's start point.

    • getWritepoint

      public Point2D.Double getWritepoint()
      The write point is the so called reference point, the start point of a glyphs base line. This is conventions in typpography. See FontMetrics for info about how this works.
      Specified by:
      getWritepoint in interface Described
      Returns:
      What does it mean that a glyph is written to a point? It means that it's base line starts at the point that this method returns.
      See Also:
      • FontMetrics

    • getAdvance

      public double getAdvance()
      The progress along a a line's baseline this glyph does when typing it. It often coincides with the width of the glyph's image width but it certainly does have to do so, concerning all serifs and for example integral limits. IThe designer of the glyph has decided this advance.
      Specified by:
      getAdvance in interface Described
      Returns:
      The advance made by the glyph when typing it.
